text:
Asha P: quick thread about a hybrid fallback model we prototyped: local "decider" on the router for emergency cuts, but with a tiny central arbitration token (CAT) that scopes what local agents can do. want to lock down failure modes.
Ben K: CAT sounds interesting. what does it contain?
Nora S: minimal: token_id, allowed_actions (cut, reduce, reroute), per-route caps, tenant_exemptions, ttl, signer_kid. signed by control-plane.
Asha P: exactly. local decider verifies CAT signature and enforces caps. control-plane rotates signer keys weekly (HSM). edges only need pub KIDs.
Ben K: signals: infra (p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, token_timeouts) => can trigger hard cuts. model-quality signals (async evals) only mark regressions and can cause traffic-shed (soft) after confirmation window.
Nora S: we also require a stability check: condition must hold for 3 consecutive samples (10s windows) before a hard cut. prevents single-window noise flipping things.
Asha P: flip-throttle: decider keeps flip_count and enforces exponential cooldown if flips exceed threshold. default: 3 flips in 10m triggers passive mode and alerts #oncall.
Ben K: what about policy rotation / revocation?
Nora S: hybrid revoke: push over ctrl-fanout + edges poll a compact PRL every 5s. if push missed PRL enforces revoke. ops UI exposes a "revoke now" button that both pushes and opens an incident.
InfraBot: reminder: emit metrics decider.token_id, decider.mode, decider.flip_count, decider.flip_reason and include token_id in traces.
Asha P: KV-warmup note: switching to fallback can produce cold KV penalties. decider will annotate events with fallback_cost_est and we accept a short spike metric. options: synchronous warm vs accept transient cost; prefer documenting and monitoring first.
Ben K: security corner-case: what if an attacker spoofs a CAT? verify signature + KID, and accept only tokens issued by CP HSM. also reject tokens with ttl < 30s to avoid churn.
Nora S: auditability: every local action writes a compact audit event to control-plane with token_id, route, action, reason, pre/post weights. if control-plane is unreachable, cache events and retry with backoff.
Asha P: idea: dry-run revokes for drills: decider logs intended actions but doesn't change routing. ops can replay logs to validate behaviour.
Ben K: testing: chaos tests that drop push messages and simulate partial revokes. assert PRL + reconciliation heals the fleet. add unit test for flip-throttle backoff.
Nora S: tenant-specific thresholds: include cohort tags in CAT so decider can apply per-tenant overrides without asking CP. small blob only.
Asha P: runbook sketch:
- passive: decider observes & logs only
- emergency: decider applies allowed hard cuts and emits incident + audit
- auto: decider can do soft-shed based on quality signals and hard-cut on infra signals
Pager: alert: decider.flip_count=4 router-edge-9 at 1825010032
Ben K: escalation: if flip_count > 3 in 10m, set decider to passive and create incident. manual override only by on-call with documented justification.
Nora S: reconciliation: decider posts compact reconcile reports every action and during periodic heartbeat so CP can rebuild last-known state. include reconcile latency metric.
Asha P: actions: Nora -> spec CAT proto + PRL format; Ben -> add chaos tests + flip-backoff unit tests; I'll draft RFC addendum and the runbook. prototype will be passive-by-default.
DeployBot: decider-passive v0.1 rolled to router-edge-9 at 1825010055 by asha
Asha P: thanks team. goal: keep emergency decisions local & fast while preserving central intent, audit, and a fast revoke path. :thumbsup:
